classification.difficultyReason: Identify midpoint and diagonal cross-sections, calculate their missing lengths, and use pyramid symmetry to convert half-angles into the requested apex angles.

content.prompt:
A right, square-based pyramid is shown below. The side lengths of the square base is $20\text{ cm}$ and the length of $AH$ is $26\text{ cm}$.

The point $P$ and $Q$ are midpoints on $AD$ and $BC$ respectively. Find the following. Give your answers correct to one decimal place.

spec.description: Unshaded right square-based pyramid with apex H above centre O, midpoints P on AD and Q on BC, and dashed midpoint and altitude construction segments.
spec.mathematics: Model vertices A=(-10,-10,0), B=(10,-10,0), C=(10,10,0), D=(-10,10,0), H=(0,0,sqrt(476)), O=(0,0,0), P=(-10,0,0), Q=(10,0,0). Faces ABCD, HAB, HBC, HCD and HDA. Projection uses x=(0.2,-0.04), y=(0.115,0.0675), z=(0,4.525/sqrt(476)); viewing direction is proportional to (0.0675,0.04,-0.0181*sqrt(476)/4.525) towards the object. Faces HAB and HBC are visible; AD, DC and HD are obscured. HP, HQ and HO retain separate construction strokes. AP=PD=BQ=QC; AB=DC. AH=26 cm and AB=20 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied dimensions, point labels, equality marks and construction lines are visible; no calculated lengths or angles.

answer.short:
$49.2^\circ$

Use the midpoint cross-section $PHQ$ and $HP=24\text{ cm}$.
answer.worked:
Since $HAP$ is right-angled at $P$, and $AP=10\text{ cm}$,
$$\begin{align*}HP^2&=26^2-10^2\\HP^2&=576\\HP&=24\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$
The centre $O$ is the midpoint of $PQ$, so $OP=10\text{ cm}$ and $HO$ bisects $\angle PHQ$.
$$\begin{align*}\sin\angle PHO&=\frac{10}{24}\\\angle PHO&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{10}{24}\right)\\\angle PHQ&=2\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{10}{24}\right)\approx49.2^\circ.\end{align*}$$

Using $QH=HP=24\text{ cm}$ from part (a), $QO=10\text{ cm}$ and $\angle PQH=\angle OQH$,
$$\begin{align*}\cos\angle OQH&=\frac{10}{24}\\\angle OQH&=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{10}{24}\right)\\\angle PQH&\approx65.4^\circ.\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$65.9^\circ$

Find the base diagonal $AC=20\sqrt2\text{ cm}$, then use the diagonal cross-section $AHC$.
answer.worked:
In the square base,
$$\begin{align*}AC&=\sqrt{20^2+20^2}\\AC&=20\sqrt2\text{ cm}\\AO&=\frac{AC}{2}=10\sqrt2\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$
Since $AH=CH$ and $HO\perp AC$, $HO$ bisects $\angle AHC$.
$$\begin{align*}\sin\angle AHO&=\frac{10\sqrt2}{26}\\\angle AHO&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{10\sqrt2}{26}\right)\\\angle AHC&=2\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{10\sqrt2}{26}\right)\approx65.9^\circ.\end{align*}$$
